title_o: How does bilingualism improve executive control? A comparison of active and reactive inhibition mechanisms.
verdict_reason: The script reads osf.io/4xs8w = Data/Colzato_et_al_replication_final.sav (32 participants, 18 + 14 by Group). The Group x Lag mixed ANOVA on T2|T1 accuracy recomputes to F(3,90) = 0.380, partial eta^2 = .0125, uncorrected p = .767, Greenhouse-Geisser p = .716. The table (p = .72, eta^2 = .01, N = 32) matches the GG-corrected p, not the uncorrected p the script's P-VALUE line prints.

data_files.notes: Code, T1 accuracy overall and per lag, Lag1/3/5/8_T2_correct (T2 given T1 correct), Raven, Vision, Group (1/2), demographics and language questionnaire. No missing values in the key columns.

data_files.path: Data/Colzato et al replication description of attentional blink analysis.txt
data_files.notes: UTF-16. Says the lag accuracies were computed in E-DataAid from per-participant E-Prime files (in Attentional Blink data.zip) and pasted into the SPSS file.
Downloaded (7.0 MB), not unpacked: E-Prime .edat2 raw files, proprietary; the aggregation step is in E-DataAid .anl files, not code.

key_test.test: mixed ANOVA (ezANOVA type 3): between Group (bilingual vs monolingual) x within Lag (1,3,5,8) on T2|T1 proportion correct; key effect = Group x Lag interaction; script also computes GG-corrected df

recompute.method: python recomputation (pingouin mixed_anova with sphericity correction)
recompute.result: Interaction F(3,90) = 0.380, p_unc = .767, p_GG = .716 (eps = .776), partial eta^2 = .0125; Lag main effect F = 56.0

obstacles: table p is the Greenhouse-Geisser value; the script's P-VALUE line prints the uncorrected p (.767), so a reproducer following the script literally gets .77
raw trials are E-Prime .edat2 (proprietary), aggregated outside code; the key test runs on the pasted per-lag proportions
R script needs ez/reshape/foreign; not run
